fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Serpent Was Never the Devil", "body": "Chance builds the whole talk out of one chapter of Godfrey Higgins's Anacalypsis, a book he says he has been reading for about two years, in which the phallus, the egg and the serpent are named the three most celebrated emblems carried in the Greek Mysteries. Reading Genesis 3:1 back against the Hebrew, he argues the word translated as subtle means cunning or crafty and also naked, so the snake carries wisdom and erotic force at once. Quoting Higgins, he contends that no unprejudiced person reading Genesis would suspect the serpent there named was the devil, and that the devil is a retroactive reading imported from Revelation."}, {"title": "Who Wrote the Ophites Into History", "body": "The Ophites reach us almost entirely through the people accusing them. Chance reads the Encyclopaedia Britannica entry on the second century Gnostic sects who, it says, treated the Jehovah of the Old Testament as a demiurge and the serpent as the true liberator of mankind, then the Jewish Encyclopedia on Irenaeus, Clement and Philaster, who placed the Ophites, Cainites and Sethites at the head of all heresies. He flags that the Nag Hammadi texts surfaced in 1947, the same year the CIA was formed, and cautions that in his view whether such groups even existed under those names is still up for debate."}, {"title": "Dylan's Case for a Mediterranean Origin", "body": "Dylan, who joined at the last minute and says he was editing chapter eleven of his book that afternoon, argues the symbol system travelled out of Italy rather than in from India. He cites a 1671 Latin inscription he found quoted in Edward Lhuyd's Archaeologia Britannica, the Etruscan city of Volterra with its so called Triton figures, and Etruscan Gorgon heads ringed with serpents. He contends the Mediterranean inscriptions all predate the oldest Indian ones, and says he will reverse his position the day someone produces older Indian ones. He also reads Elohim as plural and feminine, and Genesis 1:1 as by wisdom rather than in the beginning."}, {"title": "Gabe's Wordplay on Power and Possession", "body": "Gabe, billed as Slick Dissident, works the whole show in fragments through a five second delay and a failing connection. He traces the ladder on the Masonic tracing board to Diotima's ascent in Plato's Symposium and to the corporate habit of kissing up and kicking down, calls the letter S the letter of ownership and possession, and reads the subsection sign in law as the fine print Adam and Eve never got to. He offers Barack Obama as an anagram of obey my Cobra, links the code name Renegade to Naga, and calls Roko's basilisk a bet on what he names scientific optimism."}, {"title": "How Emblems Slowly Harden Into Idols", "body": "The last hour turns on accumulation. Chance follows Higgins's arithmetic that one new emblem per generation gives thirty emblems over ten thousand years, nobody objecting to any single addition, and traces Buddha from a plain black seated figure to the cobra hood, then the multi headed cobra, then Krishna with every absurdity Higgins could name. He asks whether the neros cycle was a deliberate fail safe, stripping the icons back every six hundred years or so, with Islam offered as a late example. Dylan answers that his objection is not that the stories are fiction, but that fiction is sold as historical fact."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight we are going to take a look at the origins and progress of religious idolatry, using the Serpent of Genesis and its symbolic meaning as our primary example. None can dispute the universality of serpent iconography in the ancient world, but what did it mean, and how was that meaning lost amidst the ever growing catalogue of icons and idols that emerged through the ages? We may see a surprise special guest or two tonight!
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Once every layer of complexity you add to it, every archetype you ascribe it to, you're now getting to this overarching very specific system that it can't be chalked up to coincidence.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Later peoples have the icons and emblems and symbols of their ancestors, but they lost the meaning of it, but they still venerate the symbol without really knowing what it really means.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The difficult thing about history is we're basically defining people, or exploring a culture, based on what we find in their cemeteries.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When you're getting caught up in good and evil, there's something possessing you that you're serving outside of yourself.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "That is exactly what happened when they ate that apple. There was the terms of the agreement that they didn't read.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The serpent is an example of how an emblem becomes an allegory, the allegory becomes an icon, and the icon becomes an idol.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The thing about all of these inscriptions that are found in the Mediterranean, they all predate the oldest inscriptions of India.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I think that Roko's basilisk is riding on scientific optimism all the way to the horizon.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "My biggest problem with all of this is not that it's fictitious. My problem with all of it is that it's being passed off as historical fact.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Religiously speaking, the literal belief in an external savior, in a historical external savior, is a step in the alchemical process of man's maturation.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Biologically we're told it's the DNA double helix, it's literally the serpent wrapping around a pole. There's the physics idea of string theory, vibrating strings or serpents making up all matter.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If we don't topple the Leviathan of the falsehoods of history, then we're just going to continue groping in the dark and playing make believe as a collective.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
